items.title: Leon Rene Interview, 1979-05-07
items.q: His drummer was the bass player. That was, you have to call him. Face up. Eddie Woods.

ctx.x: George, yeah. George Washington played, uh, uh, right with him. It was the best trumpet and trombone team in New Orleans at that time. The two, for teaming. Now he didn't play the high notes so much. He didn't go up for the screaming high notes like Kid Renee and some of the bands at that time. See, Louis had...

left I think to go to Chicago. These fellows were then taking over. Buddy had that smooth rocking style and George would kind of play along with him. And they came to California with that style. That was very good. They featured that. They didn't read music to that extent. Buddy could, but I understand that the trombone player could. So he had to go back to New Orleans when he went to Los Angeles. But in Covington, when they played. Buddy and I didn't go up to high notes, but it was mostly in that rock, I don't…

Let's see if it's working. It seems to be. We got the second reel on now. For Leon Rene. Okay, we were talking about Buddy and all that and I, but uh, and I wanted to know if he did anything about harmony at all. Harmony? Harmony? Yeah. Uh, what do you mean though? Do you think he, had ever studied any harmony? Oh, you mean, you mean, had Buddy studied harmony? Studied harmony so he could. I don't think he did. He played from a natural sound.
